title: prefill-padding-induced-regression-notes
content:
Context / quick summary:
- Observed throughput drop on hosted-api for a subset of routes (p95 latency up, overall tokens/sec down) starting ~2026-02-20 after a deployment that changed prefill/padding heuristics in the continuous batcher (PR 1024).
- Hypothesis shift: not pure batching window mis-size — looks like prefill/padding logic increased average tokens-per-request and triggered slot starvation on a few GPU pools.

Initial symptoms (what I saw):
- Grafana: tokens/sec down ~18% on model big-rl-1 across us-west pools, while incoming req/s was ~flat.
- p95 latency jumped from 180ms -> 320ms for short prompt classes (<=128 tokens).
- Queue depth metrics: more requests are waiting longer in scheduler queues, but batch sizes reduced (???).

Key idea: prefill padding (we add padding tokens to alignment when using kv-prefetch) may cause many short requests to be padded to a larger sequence length to match a warmup/prefill alignment, causing more per-request GPU work and fewer effective batches per GPU. Combined with continuous batching warmup this amplifies slot occupancy.

Commands / traces I ran (notes to self):
- kubectl -n inference logs deploy/continuous-batcher -c cbatcher --tail=400 | grep prefill
  -> saw repeated lines: "prefill_align=64 pad_to=64 prefill_tokens=48" after deploy

- promql to check average sequence length by route:
  sum(rate(model_inference_input_tokens_total{route=~"/chat/.*"}[5m])) / sum(rate(model_inference_requests_total{route=~"/chat/.*"}[5m]))
  -> avg_tokens/request increased from ~56 -> ~104 for affected routes

- curl test against staging with short prompt:
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"model":"big-rl-1","input":"hi"}' | jq .
  -> response latency 260ms (expected ~120ms)

- captured runtime log snippet (cbatcher):
  2026-02-21T14:12:04Z INFO cbatcher: building batch size=6 max_seq=128 pad_to=64 prefill_attach=true
  2026-02-21T14:12:04Z WARN cbatcher: kv_prefetch: eviction_threshold=0.75 current=0.81

- scheduler dumps: (via /debug/queue):
  route /chat/quick-summary: avg_queue_time=78ms, avg_batch_build_time=34ms, avg_batch_size=3.1

Error / odd messages I saw:
- "kv cache invalidation: entry not found for request id=..." (sporadic)
- "batch token budget exceeded: estimated=4096 available=3840" (this after padding changes)
- AssertionFailure in batch allocator: "expected contiguous slots >=6 but got 4" (rare, might be race)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Prefill alignment/padding changed from 32->64 (round up-to-64) which doubled effective seq length for many short requests: increases GPU work, reduces throughput, and increases tail latency.
2) Prefill attach enabled end-to-end for some routes: causes early KV prefetching to allocate extra cache slots and triggers eviction pressure; evictions cause extra CPU work and stalled batches.
3) Batcher warmup heuristics now favor keeping more windows open (to reduce cold-starts) which interacts badly with pad-to alignment, increasing fragmentation and preventing high-quality packing.
4) Unrelated regression: scheduler weighting update coincided with the deploy and made some GPU pools less permissive for burst—lower priority caused more queueing. (lower confidence)

Quick experiments to validate (notes):
- Roll back pad_to to 32 on a single canary pool (manual config override) and run 2h A/B. Expect avg_tokens/request to drop and tokens/sec to recover.
- Disable prefill_attach for route /chat/quick-summary in staging and compare kv eviction rates.
- Run synthetic load: 500rps of short prompts ("hi") and capture per-request seq length, batch sizes, queue_time.
- Add a quick prom alert on avg_tokens/request increase >25% to catch regressions in future.

Commands I'll run next (stateful):
- kubectl -n inference set env deploy/continuous-batcher PAD_TO=32 --record
- curl -X POST https://staging.../admin/toggle-route -d '{"route":"/chat/quick-summary","prefill_attach":false}'
- loadgen: python tools/loadgen.py --rps 500 --model big-rl-1 --prompt "hi" --duration 900 --collect-metrics

Immediate mitigation executed (what worked):
- Temporary config: pad_to=32 on two canary hosts restored tokens/sec ~+12% after 18m. p95 reduced ~40ms. That suggests pad_to change is primary.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Why did change to pad_to 64 occur? PR 1024 changed heuristics, but patch notes say "align to 64 for memory-friendly kernels" — need perf data showing net benefit.
- Need to quantify cost tradeoff: for short prompt-heavy routes, pad_to=64 increases token cost per request. Could be ok for long-job routes. Need route-level defaults.
- Is KV prefetch policy over-eager when prefill_attach=true? Need to add a guard: only prefetch if est_seq_len > threshold (e.g., >96).
- Are slot allocator assertions symptomatic of fragmentation? Add more logging around contiguous-slot avail on allocation failure.

Notes to self / voice:
- This one looked scary at first but rollback test isolates padding as the main lever. Avoid knee-jerk rollouts; instead add route-scoped defaults for pad_to and prefill_attach.
- Followups: Leila to run kernel perf tests with pad_to 64 vs 32 on big-rl-1 (per-iter token throughput). Marco to instrument allocator fragmentation metrics. I'll add a small AB test framework for pad_to per-route.

Rough timeline (for postmortem):
- 2026-02-19: deploy (PR 1024) to staging and prod canaries
- 2026-02-20 03:00 UTC: initial uptick p95 observed by Synthetic job
- 2026-02-21 14:00 UTC: broader regression; tickets created (JIRA-7813)
- 2026-02-21 15:30 UTC: pad_to rollback on canary -> partial recovery
- 2026-02-23: ongoing investigation+kernel perf tests planned

Draft mitigation plan (short):
- Short: revert pad_to change in global rollout; set route-level overrides for pad_to and prefill_attach for short-text routes.
- Medium: add heuristics to prefill: only enable attach when est_seq_len > 96; add kv cache pressure backoff.
- Long: add AB framework to test pad alignment impacts per workload and auto-tune pad_to with cost/regret minimization.

Random TODO checklist (for me):
- [ ] Add prom rule avg_tokens/request for key routes
- [ ] Push allocator extra logging and re-run canary
- [ ] Coordinate with kernel perf team for padded vs non-padded runs
- [ ] Update PR 1024 with route-scoped defaults and safe guards
- [ ] Write short postmortem once mitigations validated

End of scratchpad.
